title: The Cover of Geneva Revisited
premise: Orsen Eriksen, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent seven years burying the truth: he swapped his boarding pass with a stranger's that night, and the dead man's briefcase has been hidden in his attic ever since. When a voiceprint match to his late wife unlocks a server in Geneva, Orsen learns the briefcase holds proof of a sanctioned sabotage ring operating inside aviation safety boards — and that the ring has been hunting him for years, mistaking him for the man who was supposed to die in row twelve. To survive and expose them, Orsen must ally with the dead stranger's daughter, Ingrid, trade the evidence through a hostile intermediary in Zurich, and finally confess what he did to live. The book ends with the ring dismantled by public inquiry, Ingrid forgiving him at her father's grave, and Orsen unpacking the go-bag for good.
about_author: Marguerite Ishikawa is a former airline safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. She lives between Copenhagen and Kyoto, where she collects vintage luggage tags from flights that never crashed.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Seven years after the crash, Orsen inspects wreckage for the safety board while privately maintaining a packed go-bag and rehearsing his alibi. A routine anniversary memorial triggers flashbacks of the seat swap. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. An encrypted alert arrives: a server in Geneva has been unlocked using a voiceprint sample of his dead wife, Lena, harvested from old voicemails. Someone is impersonating her. He opens the attic briefcase for the first time since the funeral. Beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: Ingrid Halvorsen
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. In Oslo, Ingrid receives an anonymous message claiming her father didn't die by accident — and that a man named Eriksen knows why. She flies to Copenhagen to confront the stranger whose name was on her father's ticket. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen and Ingrid meet at the memorial wall; she recognizes him from the passenger manifest photo. He lies badly; she notices. They part as adversaries, each now certain the other is lying. Beat: two liars circling one truth.

chapters.title: What the Briefcase Holds
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Forced open properly, the briefcase reveals a second identity, ledgers of payments routed through a Geneva trust, and a microcassette naming three safety-board officials. Orsen realizes the sabotage ring thinks HE is the courier they killed. Beat: the lie becomes a target on his back.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Amager
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Ingrid tails Orsen through Copenhagen and witnesses a black sedan following him too — professionals. When she warns him, their wary alliance forms out of necessity. Beat: enemies forced into partnership.

chapters.title: The First Death
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A retired board auditor who once handled the ledger is found dead in Malmö, staged as suicide. Orsen recognizes the staging technique from crash-site forensics. The ring is erasing the paper trail — and he is next. Beat: stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Geneva Calling
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. The anonymous messenger contacts Ingrid directly: it's a whistleblower inside the Geneva trust, code-named VESTA, who confirms the voiceprint was bait to flush out whoever holds the briefcase. Ingrid must decide whether to hand Orsen over. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Confession at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cornered by Ingrid's questions, Orsen confesses the seat swap — that her father gave him the ticket deliberately, knowing something was wrong with the flight, and asked him to carry the case if he lived. Beat: shame transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Instructions
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Replaying her father's last voicemail with new ears, Ingrid decodes his references to 'the Geneva account' and a dead-drop protocol. Her father chose Orsen not randomly but because he was the only investigator who couldn't be bought. Beat: grief reframed as trust.

chapters.title: VESTA Unmasked
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Meeting VESTA's cutout in Hamburg, they learn the whistleblower is Lena's former colleague — and that Lena had discovered the ring weeks before the flight. Her death wasn't collateral; it was scheduled. Beat: rage crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ring's fixer, Callas, makes contact: full immunity and a new life in exchange for the briefcase and silence. He gives Orsen 72 hours. Orsen pretends to consider. Beat: temptation wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. The pair go dark in a safehouse, copying and dispersing the ledger to journalists as insurance. Paranoia frays them — Orsen nearly bolts with the go-bag. Ingrid talks him down. Beat: the survival instinct versus the truth.

chapters.title: The Journalist Problem
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Their chosen journalist turns up compromised; a leaked draft reaches Callas within hours. They realize there's a mole inside VESTA's network. Trust collapses to just the two of them and a dead man's instructions. Beat: isolation sharpening focus.

chapters.title: The Zurich Intermediary
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Following the drop protocol, they arrange the trade through Herr Brandt, a discreet Zurich banker who handled the trust. Brandt agrees to authenticate the ledger publicly — for a price: the original cassette, no copies. Beat: bargaining with the past.

chapters.title: Ambush on the Limmat
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The handoff is ambushed by Callas's team; Brandt is killed, the cassette seemingly lost, and Orsen wounded escaping across the river with Ingrid. But the ambush proves the ring fears exposure more than the evidence itself. Beat: despair seeding defiance.

chapters.title: The Copy That Matters
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Revealed: the 'lost' cassette was a decoy Orsen prepared years ago; the real recording is embedded in the flight data recorder archive from 4471 itself, hidden in plain sight in official records. Beat: the investigator's craft becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Reopening Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Using board credentials one last time, Orsen files to reopen the 4471 investigation, attaching the decoded FDR anomalies. The safety board fractures; officials named in the ledger scramble; VESTA goes public. Beat: the machine turning on its makers.

chapters.title: Callas's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Callas corners Orsen aboard a delayed flight out of Zurich, offering one final trade. Orsen refuses aloud, in front of witnesses, choosing exposure over escape. Callas is detained when the reopened inquiry names him. Beat: the go-bag finally set down.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Public hearings unfold; testimony about row twelve becomes national news. Orsen testifies to everything, including the seat swap, surrendering his career and reputation. Beat: truth as penance, freely paid.

chapters.title: The Grave in Oslo
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At her father's grave, Ingrid tells Orsen he was the heir her father chose, and forgives him — not for surviving, but for carrying it alone so long. They place the empty briefcase at the headstone. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Epilogue. Months later, Orsen unpacks the go-bag item by item, keeping only Lena's voicemail and a new boarding pass — seat 12A, voluntarily booked, a flight he chooses to take. Beat: survival redeemed as living.
